Subject: Intermittent 429/500s and p99 latency spikes in production (urgent)

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in 429 throttles and 500 errors around 15:30 PT today during our nightly batch scoring window. P99 latency jumped to ~4.8s for text-generation calls and several jobs failed with 429s mid-run. Our SRE captured logs and a call-stack sample (attached). This is impacting our end-of-day processing and downstream reports.

Things we've observed:
- Errors correlate with short bursts of high request rate (100s of parallel scoring jobs).
- Prior to today we've been within our committed qps but use burst capacity; we don't expect sustained throttling.
- No config changes on our side in the last 48 hours.

Could you confirm if Redwood applied any platform changes or if there's an ongoing degradation? We need a timeline and mitigation ASAP — our execs are asking for status.

Investigating — initial findings below. Short summary: we have an edge-case in our quota + burst policy evaluation that misclassifies these parallel short-lived scoring jobs as sustained bursts and routes them into the conservative rate-limited path. That triggers token throttles and elevated queuing which shows up to customers as 429s and high p99 latency.

What I see so far (quick notes):
- Reproduced with FinApps sample: when 200 parallel short-lived connections start within ~60s, the server interprets the pattern as a sustained surge because the burst-window smoothing uses a 60s decay and the burst-credit regen was disabled for this account due to a stale flag.
- Regression introduced by config rollout 2026-02-28 (burst-policy runtime patch) — rollout toggled a per-account override guard that ended up disabling regen for some legacy accounts.
- Our autoscaler and routing still healthy; this is policy-level throttling, not GPU saturation.

Immediate mitigations proposed (short window):
1) Emergency per-account quota bump + manual restore of burst-credit regen for FinApps (10 min ops change) — will stop throttles quickly.
2) Insert temporary routing fallback to cached model variant for high-concurrency calls from their API key — reduces impact on live tokens.
3) Roll a hotfix to revert the per-account override and enable retro-active regen application (1-3 hours).

I'll open PROD-921 with full reproducer and timeline, attach logs and a screenshot of the policy evaluation. If owners agree, I can apply the emergency change now.

Vivek
Head of Engineering, Serving Runtime
